idiom_name: one factory class or module of named creation methods returning valid objects
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: keep one mother per domain class or aggregate (CustomerMother, InvoiceMother) whose methods return fully constructed, invariant-satisfying instances named after the business scenario they represent ('a customer who just signed up') rather than after their fields. Every call must build a fresh object graph, because a cached instance turns client tests into users of a shared mutable fixture. Start with a small set of canonical examples and let tests adjust the one detail they assert on; when adjustments multiply, layer a Test Data Builder or a generator underneath instead of adding more factory methods. The mother lives in test code only.
pitfalls: Skipping the mother in some tests: ad-hoc construction next to canned fixtures drifts and defeats the single point of change.
Returning shared instances instead of fresh objects, so one test's mutation becomes another test's surprise.
Letting the mother grow a method per variation instead of introducing a builder once variation is the dominant need.

Wrong move: use a mother to hide oversized unit-test setup -> the test passes only because a large realistic graph is buried behind the factory and coupling remains hidden -> instead fix the coupling or use a focused builder or abstraction, reserving mothers for shared acceptance or integration scenarios.

Wrong move: turn a mother into an all-purpose random-data generator -> generated values erase the shared business vocabulary and make failures harder to reproduce -> instead keep named fixtures deterministic and use a separate seeded generator for broad variation.
